title: The Pass Where Wind Learns to Turn

features.name: the-turning-point
features.desc-on-touch: Where wind meets itself coming from opposite directions and learns it has been singing. The pass is alive with the moment of realization.

features.name: lichen-chorus-field
features.desc-on-touch: Rows of slow-growth colour scattered across the high stone. Each lichen has learned that wind carries the other's song.

features.name: alpine-memory
features.desc-on-touch: A stone carving that the wind has been reading for centuries. The carving has learned the wind's touch the way stone learns pressure.

features.name: gathered-weather
features.desc-on-touch: Wind patterns frozen in form, a stack of air-currents that learned to hold themselves still enough to be seen.

features.name: the-bifurcation
features.desc-on-touch: Where one wind becomes two, learning that turning is just another kind of singing. Split breath makes harmony.

features.name: alpine-receiver
features.desc-on-touch: A burl where the hardware listens to wind frequencies. The tree has learned that the wind has been trying to speak all along.

reverie.title: REVERIE — high pass at the turning
narr: She pointed to where the wind from two valleys collided and
made a sound neither valley alone could make. You both stood at
the turning point, the place wind learns it has a voice. She said
the archive is like this: all the contradictions meeting at one
high place and learning to sing together. The altitude made it

inscription: here the wind has learned that turning is the highest form of listening
